en: to blink; to flicker; to flash

examples.en: The baby looked at me, blinking.
The car ahead went slowly with its hazard lights blinking.
A small light is flickering far away.
Every time I blinked, sleepiness washed over me.
I looked for a long time at the night sky with twinkling stars.

examples.ko: 눈에 먼지가 들어가서 눈을 자꾸 깜박였어요.
examples.en: Dust got in my eye, so I kept blinking.

explain: '깜박거리다'와 비슷하지만 '눈을 깜박이다'처럼 목적어를 받아 쓸 수 있어요. 운전할 때 방향지시등을 '깜빡이'라고도 말해요. '깜빡이다'로도 쓰는 같은 말이에요.

phrases.en: Stars are twinkling in the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깜박이다'와 같은 말이고 둘 다 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word as the head word, and both spellings are fine.

phrases.en: I looked at the twinkling star for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' ending modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 사진 찍을 때 눈을 깜박이지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't blink when the photo is taken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적어 '눈을'과 함께 쓰는 금지 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A prohibition used with the object '눈을'.

explain_en: Short quick blink of eyes or signal lights (방향등이 깜박이다) It is similar to '깜박거리다' but can take an object, as in '눈을 깜박이다'. When driving, people also call the turn signal '깜빡이'. '깜빡이다' is another spelling of the same word.

t90.ax: The baby looked at me, blinking.

en: to farm; to do farm work

examples.en: My parents still farm in the countryside.
Grandfather sent me rice that he grew himself.

examples.ko: 사막화로 농사짓던 땅을 잃은 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are losing the land they used to farm because of desertification.
It's hard to farm because there is no rain.
I had no land to farm, so I came to the city.

examples.ko: 우리 이웃은 산 밑에서 농사지으며 살아요.
examples.en: Our neighbor lives farming at the foot of the mountain.

explain: '짓다'는 ㅅ 불규칙이라서 '지어요', '지은', '지을'처럼 ㅅ이 빠져요. '농사를 짓다'처럼 띄어 써도 되고, 한 단어로 붙여서 '농사짓다'라고 써도 돼요. 쌀이나 고추처럼 작물을 쓸 때는 '고추 농사를 짓다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My grandmother farms a small field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띄어 써도 되고 목적어 '농사를'을 넣어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can be written separately, with 농사를 as the object.

phrases.en: Last year I farmed in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 말할 때 'ㅅ'이 빠져서 '농사지었어요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the past tense the ㅅ drops, giving 농사지었어요.

phrases.en: My father grows chili peppers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 작물 이름을 붙여 무엇을 키우는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a crop name in front to say what is being grown.

explain_en: '짓다' is an ㅅ-irregular verb, so the ㅅ drops in forms like '지어요', '지은' and '지을'. You can write it spaced as '농사를 짓다' or as one word, '농사짓다'. With a crop such as rice or peppers, '고추 농사를 짓다' sounds natural.

examples.en: This is my regular place that I go to often.
I have a regular spot near my office.
At my regular place, the owner gives me extra side dishes.

examples.ko: 이사 가서 단골집을 바꿔야 해서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: I moved, so I have to change my regular place, which is a shame.
I went to my usual place with a friend and had soft tofu stew.
The owner of my regular place remembers my name.

explain: 식당, 미용실, 카페처럼 자주 가는 가게에 두루 쓰지만 식당에 가장 많이 써요. '단골 식당', '단골 가게'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: It's our family's regular restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 가는 곳이 식당이라는 것을 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear that the place is a restaurant.

phrases.en: This bakery is my regular shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이 아닌 가게에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for shops other than restaurants too.

phrases.example: 한 번 갔는데 바로 단골집이 됐어요.
phrases.en: I went once and it immediately became my regular place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 가게 된 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place you end up visiting often.

explain_en: It covers restaurants, hair salons and cafés, though it is most common for restaurants. People also say it in parts, like '단골 식당' or '단골 가게'.

examples.en: The child regretted having stolen from the store.
He was so hungry that he stole some bread.
If you steal other people's things, you get punished.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어제 옆집에서 도둑질하다가 잡혔어요.
examples.en: That person was caught yesterday while stealing from the next-door house.

examples.ko: 도둑질해서 번 돈은 쓰고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to spend money earned by stealing.
Don't steal; that belongs to your friend.

explain: '훔치다'는 '지갑을 훔치다'처럼 물건 하나를 몰래 가져가는 행동이에요. '도둑질하다'는 도둑 같은 짓을 한다는 느낌이 강해서 나쁜 행동이라고 말하는 분위기가 있어요. '도둑질을 하다'처럼 나누어 쓸 수도 있어요.

phrases.en: Someone stole my bicycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 하나를 몰래 가져가는 행동에 써요. 도둑질하다보다 덜 강하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for secretly taking one item; it sounds less strong than 도둑질하다.

phrases.en: That person stole from a shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도둑질하다'를 나누어 쓴 말이에요. 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A split form of 도둑질하다; the meaning is the same.

phrases.en: You must not steal other people's things.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면 안 되다'는 하지 말라는 뜻이에요. 규칙이나 가르침을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-(으)면 안 되다' means 'must not'; used for rules and lessons.

explain_en: Plain everyday word for the act of stealing as a crime. '훔치다' is quietly taking one item, as in '지갑을 훔치다'. '도둑질하다' has the feel of doing what a thief does, so it carries a tone of calling the act bad. It can also be split as '도둑질을 하다'.

t90.ax: Don't steal; that belongs to your friend.

en: alumnus; schoolmate; classmate from the same school

examples.en: Today I met a high school classmate after a long time.
Yesterday I went to a university classmate's wedding.
For the first time in a while, former classmates got together for dinner.
I ran into an elementary school classmate on the street.
That person is my middle school classmate.

examples.ko: 이번 주 동창생 모임에 같이 가실래요?
examples.en: Would you like to come to the alumni gathering this week?

explain: 같은 학교를 다닌 사이를 말하고, 줄여서 '동창'이라고도 많이 해요. '고등학교 동창생'처럼 학교 이름을 앞에 붙여서 써요. 같은 해에 입학하거나 입사한 사람은 '동기'라고 해서 달라요.

phrases.en: I'm meeting a schoolmate this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동창생'을 줄인 말로 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 동창생 used more in daily speech.

phrases.en: I'm still in touch with a classmate from elementary school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 이름을 앞에 붙여 어느 학교인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the school name first to say which school.

phrases.en: I'm going to my high school reunion this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동창생들이 모이는 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The gathering where alumni meet.

explain_en: People who graduated from or attended the same school, often years later. It refers to people who went to the same school, and it is often shortened to '동창'. You usually put the school level in front, as in '고등학교 동창생'. People who entered a school or company in the same year are '동기', which is different.

examples.en: The wizard waved his staff.
A kind wizard appears in that movie.
When I was little, I wanted to become a wizard.

examples.ko: 주문을 외운 뒤에 마법사는 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: After reciting the spell, the wizard opened the door.
I went to the party in a wizard hat.
The wizard in the fairy tale helped the princess.

explain: '마법사'는 마법을 쓰는 사람을 두루 부르는 말이고, '마녀'는 여자 마법사를 가리켜요. 게임에서는 직업 이름으로도 써요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '마법을 쓰다', '마법을 걸다'예요.

phrases.en: The wizard used magic to open the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마법사가 하는 행동을 말할 때 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for what a wizard does.

phrases.en: The wizard cast a spell on the prince.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가에게 마법의 효과를 입힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting a spell on someone.

phrases.en: A witch lives in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마법사' 중에서 여자를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers specifically to a female magic user.

explain_en: '마법사' is the general word for a person who uses magic, while '마녀' means a witch, a female one. It is also used as a class name in games. Common partners are '마법을 쓰다' (use magic) and '마법을 걸다' (cast a spell).

examples.en: I took a hand mirror out of my bag and checked my hair.

examples.ko: 이 손거울은 작아서 가방에 쏙 들어가요.
examples.en: This hand mirror is small, so it fits right in a bag.
At the hair salon, they showed me the back of my hair with a hand mirror.
The hand mirror broke, so I have to buy a new one.
I always carry at least one hand mirror.
Sunlight is reflecting off the hand mirror on the desk.

explain: 손에 들거나 가지고 다닐 수 있는 작은 거울이에요. 벽에 걸거나 서서 전신을 비추는 거울은 '거울'이나 '전신거울'이라고 해요. '손'이 붙은 말은 '손수건, 손전등'처럼 들고 쓰는 물건을 자주 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 가방에 작은 손거울을 하나 넣고 다녀요.
phrases.en: I carry a small hand mirror in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기가 작다는 점을 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress that it is small.

phrases.en: I fixed my makeup while looking in a hand mirror.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴이나 머리를 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking your face or hair.
phrases.en_equiv: to look in a hand mirror

phrases.en: I checked the back of my head with a hand mirror.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 안 보이는 곳을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to check a spot that is hard to see.
phrases.en_equiv: to check with a hand mirror

explain_en: It is a small mirror you hold in your hand or carry around. Mirrors hung on walls or showing your whole body are '거울' or '전신거울'. Words with '손' often refer to things you hold and use, like '손수건' and '손전등'.

examples.en: I am going to see my mother this weekend.
My mother sent me some kimchi.
After I had the baby, my mother helped me a lot.
My mother farms in our hometown.
It is my mother's birthday, so I bought a gift.
I went to the market with my mother.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 어머니를 시댁과 구분해서 말할 때 써요. 짝말은 '시어머니'(남편의 어머니)예요. 남편이 아내의 어머니를 말할 때는 '장모님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My mom made side dishes for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '친정어머니'보다 편하고 정다운 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warmer, more casual way to say it than 'chinjeong-eomeoni'.

phrases.en: I called my mother in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '께'와 '드리다'로 높이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the honorific particle and verb to show respect.

phrases.en: I look a lot like my mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴이나 성격이 어머니와 비슷할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your looks or personality resemble your mother's.

explain_en: A married woman uses it to talk about her own mother as distinct from her husband's family. The counterpart is '시어머니' (husband's mother). A husband calls his wife's mother '장모님'.

examples.en: On the way home from work I bought a whole fried chicken.

examples.ko: 시장에서 산 통닭이 정말 바삭하고 맛있어요.
examples.en: The whole fried chicken I bought at the market is really crispy and tasty.
On payday my father came home with a whole fried chicken.

examples.ko: 통닭 한 마리를 가족이 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: My family shared one whole fried chicken.
The fried chicken shop at the market always has a long line.
They say that in the old days people ate whole fried chicken on every birthday.

explain: 요즘은 보통 '치킨'이라고 말해요. '통닭'은 한 마리를 통째로 튀기거나 구운 옛날식 느낌이 있어서 시장이나 부모님 세대가 자주 써요. 세는 말은 '한 마리'예요.

phrases.en: Tonight we will order chicken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘은 '통닭'보다 '치킨'을 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nowadays 'chicken' is used more often than 'tongdak'.

phrases.en: I bought one whole fried chicken at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닭은 '한 마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Chickens are counted with 'one mari'.

phrases.en: My father bought fried chicken on the way home from work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날식 느낌이 있어서 부모님 세대가 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It has an old-fashioned feel and is often used by the parents' generation.

explain_en: These days most people just say 'chicken' (치킨). 'Tongdak' has an old-fashioned feel of a whole bird fried or roasted, so you hear it at traditional markets and from the parents' generation. The counter is '한 마리' (one bird).

examples.en: The child fell asleep early in pajamas.
The pajamas were so comfy that I wore them all day.
I went to the convenience store in my pajamas.
The new pajamas are cotton, so they are very soft.

examples.ko: 파자마도 챙겼어요? 오늘 자고 갈 거잖아요.
examples.en: Did you pack pajamas too? You're staying over tonight.
I accidentally spilled coffee on my pajamas.

explain: '잠옷'은 잘 때 입는 옷 전체를 말해요. 파자마는 그중에서 윗옷과 바지가 따로 있는 옷을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The pajama pants are comfortable, so I wear them at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파자마의 아래옷만 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about only the bottom half of pajamas.

phrases.en: I slept in my sleepwear.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파자마'보다 넓은 말로, 잘 때 입는 모든 옷이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 'pajamas' for anything you sleep in.

phrases.en: My younger sibling came out in pajamas.
phrases.nuance_ko: '차림'은 옷을 입은 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '차림' describes how someone looks in their clothes.

explain_en: '잠옷' covers any clothes worn for sleeping. 파자마 is the kind with a separate top and pants.

t90.ax: The child fell asleep early in pajamas.

examples.ko: 동지에는 팥죽을 먹는 풍습이 지금도 있어요.
examples.en: The custom of eating red bean porridge on the winter solstice still exists today.

examples.ko: 팥죽에 설탕을 넣어서 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people add sugar to their red bean porridge.
Red bean porridge tastes best when eaten warm.
I miss the red bean porridge my grandmother used to cook.

examples.ko: 팥죽 한 그릇 먹고 나니 몸이 따뜻해졌어요.
examples.en: After a bowl of red bean porridge, my body warmed up.
I'm going to have red bean porridge for lunch today.

explain: 팥으로 쑨 죽이고, 동지에 먹는 음식으로 유명해요. 붉은 팥이 나쁜 기운을 쫓는다고 믿었기 때문이에요. 죽은 '쑤다'라는 동사를 써서 '팥죽을 쑤다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My mother made red bean porridge on the winter solstice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 죽을 만들 때는 '만들다'보다 '쑤다'를 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For porridge, 쑤다 is used more than 만들다.

phrases.en: On a cold day I ate warm red bean porridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 일을 말하는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to talk about eating it.

phrases.en: Rice balls go into the solstice red bean porridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동지에 먹는 팥죽을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the red bean porridge eaten on the winter solstice.

explain_en: It is porridge made from red beans and is famous as a food eaten on the winter solstice, because red beans were believed to drive away bad luck. For porridge you can use the verb '쑤다', as in '팥죽을 쑤다' (to cook red bean porridge).

examples.en: On the way home from school, I ate tteokbokki with a friend.
It rained, so the way home from school was a mess.
Children's way home from school must be safe.
I bought ice cream at the convenience store on my way home from school.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 하굣길마다 같은 골목을 지났어요.
examples.en: As a child, I passed the same alley every day on the way home.
Cherry blossoms are in full bloom along the way home from school.

explain: 학교에 갈 때는 '등굣길', 집에 돌아올 때는 '하굣길'이라고 해서 짝으로 외우면 좋아요. '-길'은 '그때 가는 길'이라는 느낌이라 '퇴근길', '출근길'과 같은 방식으로 써요.

phrases.en: The way to school is crowded with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 갈 때의 길이라서 하굣길과 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The road to school, paired with 하굣길.

phrases.en: I stopped by a bookstore on my way home from school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에 가는 길에 어딘가에 잠깐 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you stop somewhere briefly on the way home.
phrases.en_equiv: to stop by on the way home from school

phrases.en: I met my teacher on my way home from school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 누군가를 만났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you run into someone on the way.
phrases.en_equiv: to meet on the way home

explain_en: The pair is '등굣길' (way to school) and '하굣길' (way home from school), so learn them together. The ending '-길' gives a sense of the route you take at that time, just like '출근길' and '퇴근길'.

en: to sway; to swing; to rock

examples.en: The wind is blowing and the branches are swaying.
This desk has a wobbly leg, so it's uncomfortable.
The child's front tooth has started to wobble.

examples.ko: 버스가 흔들거릴 때 손잡이를 꼭 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold the handle tight when the bus sways.

examples.ko: 배가 계속 흔들거리니까 속이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The boat keeps rocking, so my stomach feels bad.
Please don't swing your legs while sitting on the chair.

explain: '흔들리다'와 비슷한데, 흔들거리다는 가볍게 자꾸 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 흔들리는 이나 책상 다리처럼 헐거워서 움직이는 것에도 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Don't sit on the wobbly chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' ending lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 다리가 튼튼해서 이 책상은 흔들거리지 않아요.
phrases.en: This desk has sturdy legs, so it doesn't wobble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 튼튼하고 안정적이라는 말을 할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form tells you something is sturdy and stable.

phrases.en: The leaves sway in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. 흔들거리다보다 흔들리는 모습을 두루 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that describes shaking more generally than 흔들거리다.

explain_en: General shaking or swaying of objects that are loose or hanging (나뭇가지가 흔들거리다) It is close to '흔들리다', but 흔들거리다 describes something moving lightly and repeatedly. It also fits loose things like a wobbly tooth or a table leg.

t90.ax: Hold the handle tight when the bus sways.
